cues.en: While we're still operating under our bleeding edge alert, let's briefly cover a few more recent research topics that are worth keeping an eye on.
cues.zh: 還在前沿研究提醒環節，簡單介紹幾個值得留意的新研究主題。

cues.en: Some people have applied a neural network model called word2vec to recommender problems.
cues.zh: 有人把 word2vec 神經網路模型，用於推薦。

cues.en: If you have text data to work with, it can be an interesting tool.
cues.zh: 有文字資料時，是有趣工具。

cues.en: The idea is you start with some words that represent the context or user history you want to use to inform your recommendations, but to make it easier to understand let's just start with the problem
cues.zh: 概念是，從代表情境或使用者歷史的詞出發，用來推薦；但為了容易理解，先看

cues.en: of completing someone's sentence.
cues.zh: 替人接完句子的問題。

cues.en: We can encode all of the words in that sentence, feed it through an embedding layer and a hidden layer where the learning takes place, and run a softmax classifier on the output of the hidden layer
cues.zh: 將句中所有詞編碼，送入嵌入層、學習的隱藏層，再對隱藏輸出做 softmax 分類，

cues.en: to find the probabilities of each word that might be associated with the ones you fed in as input.
cues.zh: 找出各詞與輸入詞相關的機率。

cues.en: In this example, we feed in signals associated with the words to boldly go where no one has, and a properly trained word2vec network might classify the word gone
cues.zh: 這個例子，輸入 to boldly go where no one has，訓練好的 word2vec，可能將 gone，

cues.en: as the most likely word associated with those words.
cues.zh: 分類為最可能相關的詞。

cues.en: An example of applying this technique to a recommender system would be recommending menu items to restaurant owners, based on the menus of other restaurant owners.
cues.zh: 用於推薦的例子，是根據其他餐廳菜單，向餐廳老闆推薦菜色。

cues.en: Perhaps you could train word2vec with a large number of menus and the words that appear on them.
cues.zh: 也許用大量菜單及上面的詞，訓練 word2vec。

cues.en: Then, by feeding in the words in a specific restaurant's menu, you could recommend terms associated with other dishes they might want to offer on their menu.
cues.zh: 輸入某餐廳菜單的詞，就能推薦與其他可供應菜色相關的詞。

cues.en: You might observe that this is also the sort of problem recurrent neural networks, or RNNs, are made for, and you would be correct.
cues.zh: 可能發現，這也適合 RNN，沒錯。

cues.en: There is also research in using RNNs for text-based recommendations, like the menu item recommender we just mentioned.
cues.zh: 也有研究用 RNN 做文字推薦，像剛才菜色推薦。

cues.en: Things get interesting when you use word2vec with things that aren't words at all.
cues.zh: word2vec 用在根本不是詞的東西時，更有趣。

cues.en: In one interesting example, a streaming music service called Anghami used word2vec, but applied it to the problem of recommending songs based on a user's previous choices in their system.
cues.zh: 例如，串流音樂服務 Anghami，用 word2vec，根據使用者先前選擇推薦歌曲。

cues.en: It works exactly the same way as it does with words in sentences, but instead of working with words in sentences, it works with individual songs that are part of someone's stream.
cues.zh: 與句中詞完全相同，但處理的，是串流裡個別歌曲。

cues.en: The output isn't a prediction of words, but of other songs that fit into the sentence of that user's past stream of songs.
cues.zh: 輸出不是詞預測，而是適合接進使用者過去歌曲「句子」的其他歌曲。

cues.en: This is a really neat example of taking an established idea, and getting an entirely new system just by questioning the assumptions about what it's for.
cues.zh: 很棒的例子：只要質疑既有想法的用途假設，就能得到全新系統。

cues.en: An interesting paper in the 2017 RecSys conference proposed using 3D convolutional neural networks for session-based recommendations.
cues.zh: 2017 年 RecSys 研討會，有篇有趣論文，提出用三維 CNN 做工作階段推薦。

cues.en: We talked about using recurrent neural networks to produce session-based recommendations.
cues.zh: 前面談過 RNN 工作階段推薦。

cues.en: This idea is basically adding two more dimensions that can be used to consider feature data about the items being recommended in addition to the data on how they were consumed in peoples' clickstreams.
cues.zh: 這想法基本上，多加兩維，除了點擊流消費行為，也考慮推薦項目的特徵資料。

cues.en: All of the feature data is character-encoded, and then we treat it just like we would treat image data when using a CNN and trying to do image recognition.
cues.zh: 特徵資料全部做字元編碼，再當成 CNN 影像辨識時的影像資料。

cues.en: As you can imagine, this gets very complicated, very quickly.
cues.zh: 可想而知，很快變非常複雜。

cues.en: The one saving grace is that CNNs themselves are in widespread use these days in other fields, so the complexity of the CNN itself is sort of a solved problem.
cues.zh: 好處是，CNN 在其他領域已廣泛使用，本身複雜性，大致已有解法。

cues.en: There are lots of little twists involved with applying it to clickstream sessions, however, such as how to deal with sessions of different lengths.
cues.zh: 但用於點擊流，仍很多變化，例如不同長度工作階段。

cues.en: CNNs want to work with blocks of data that are all the same size, which presents a problem the paper has to address.
cues.zh: CNN 想處理相同大小區塊，所以論文要解決。

cues.en: Complexity aside, it's hard to argue with their results.
cues.zh: 撇開複雜性，結果難以否認。

cues.en: They did outperform RNNs pretty handily in their paper, but we have to remember this is a solution for a very specific kind of problem.
cues.zh: 論文中，明顯勝過 RNN，但記得，只解特定問題。

cues.en: Recommending items in a clickstream session, taking content attributes into account at the same time.
cues.zh: 在點擊流工作階段推薦，同時考慮內容屬性。

cues.en: The paper for this idea is also available for free online if you'd like to learn more.
cues.zh: 想學更多，論文也有免費線上版本。

cues.en: Again, it's just something to keep in the back of your head for now.
cues.zh: 目前只需記在心裡。

cues.en: You're not going to find examples of how to code this up online yet because it's just too new.
cues.zh: 因為太新，還找不到線上程式範例。

cues.en: A more straightforward application of CNNs in the world of recommender systems is using them to extract feature data from the things themselves that you are trying to recommend.
cues.zh: CNN 在推薦系統中，更直接的用法，是從待推薦事物本身，擷取特徵。

cues.en: For example, just like you can use a convolutional neural network to classify an image as, say, a duck, you can also use a CNN to classify an audio waveform as a specific musical genre.
cues.zh: 例如，能用 CNN 把影像分為鴨子，也能把音訊波形分成特定曲風。

cues.en: If you're building a music recommendation system, you might not have good metadata about the songs you need to recommend but you could use a CNN to extract that metadata, such as the genre, automatically.
cues.zh: 建立音樂推薦時，可能沒有好的歌曲中繼資料，但能用 CNN，自動擷取曲風等資訊。

cues.en: That genre information could then work its way into a content-based recommendation scheme of some sort, that might augment a collaborative filtering or matrix factorization model.
cues.zh: 再把類型資訊，加入某種內容式推薦，補充協同過濾或矩陣分解模型。

cues.en: You could even imagine using a CNN to classify paintings, and recommend paintings to people based on the types of paintings they've liked in the past.
cues.zh: 甚至能用 CNN 分類畫作，再根據過去喜歡的畫作類型推薦。

cues.en: You still need to train your CNNs, so you can't use them to create new classifications it's never seen before but it can be a useful tool in filling in attribute information
cues.zh: 仍需要訓練 CNN，不能建立從沒看過的新分類，但可用來補齊

cues.en: for new items or items with missing data.
cues.zh: 新項目、缺失資料項目的屬性。

cues.en: That wraps up our bleeding edge alert on deep learning in recommender systems, but research is progressing quickly on this front.
cues.zh: 推薦深度學習的前沿提醒，到這裡，但研究進展很快。

cues.en: By the time you watch this, some of these ideas may already be mainstream.
cues.zh: 你看到時，一些想法可能已成主流。

cues.en: We know YouTube and Amazon already have systems in production using deep learning for recommendations, and are starting to publish their learnings from it.
cues.zh: 知道 YouTube、Amazon，正式環境已有深度學習推薦，也開始發表經驗。

cues.en: It's exciting times in the field of recommender systems but remember, don't get caught up in the hype just for the sake of it.
cues.zh: 推薦領域正令人興奮，但別只為熱門，就陷入炒作。

cues.en: For many problems, older, simpler solutions are still a better fit.
cues.zh: 很多問題，較舊、較簡單方案，仍更適合。
